senses.gloss: Proved to work over a long period of use.
examples: She uses a *time-tested* recipe for the holidays.
The company stuck with its *time-tested* approach.
His advice is simple and *time-tested*.

position: attributive only — *a timed test*; after a verb it is the passive verb, not the adjective

senses.gloss: Done under a set time limit, or set to happen at a fixed time.
examples: The final is a *timed* test — fifty minutes, no extensions.
The sprinklers run on a *timed* cycle.
We did a *timed* run to see how long the drive takes.

senses.gloss: Not affected by the passing of time; always in style.
examples: A plain black dress is *timeless*.
The movie has a *timeless* quality.
Nothing looks *more timeless* than a white shirt and jeans.

senses.gloss: Easily frightened and not confident.
examples: He was too *timid* to raise his hand in class.
A *timid* little dog hid under the couch.
She's *more timid* about calling strangers than her sister is.

contrast: Formal and literary. In speech Americans say *timid* or *nervous*.

senses.gloss: Nervous and easily frightened.
examples: There was a *timorous* knock on the door.
Her voice was *timorous* at first.
The *timorous* new hire barely spoke in meetings.

senses.gloss: Feeling or causing a light prickling on the skin.
examples: I had a *tingling* feeling in my fingers.
My foot fell asleep and now it's *tingling*.
The mint gives the balm a *tingling* coolness.

senses.gloss: Sounding thin and metallic, like a cheap speaker.
examples: The phone's speaker sounds *tinny*.
*Tinny* music played from an old radio in the corner.
The laptop speakers are even *tinnier* than the phone.

contrast: *Tipsy* is mild and friendly — a glass or two. *Drunk* is much stronger.

senses.gloss: Slightly drunk.
examples: After two glasses of wine she was a little *tipsy*.
A few *tipsy* guests were singing in the yard.
He gets *tipsier* faster than anyone I know.

senses.gloss: Working on and on without getting tired or giving up.
examples: She was a *tireless* advocate for the students.
His *tireless* work on the case finally paid off.
Nobody is *more tireless* than our volunteer coordinator.

contrast: *Tiresome* means boring and annoying, not physically tiring — for that say *tiring*.

senses.gloss: Boring and annoying.
examples: His jokes get *tiresome* after a while.
We sat through a *tiresome* speech about parking.
Filling out the same form twice is *more tiresome* than it sounds.

contrast: Lowercase for the adjective. Capitalized, *Titanic* is the ship.

senses.gloss: Enormous in size, strength or effort.
examples: It took a *titanic* effort to finish on time.
The two teams fought a *titanic* battle in the final.
They faced *titanic* problems in the first year.

senses.gloss: Mildly exciting, usually in a sexual or gossipy way.
examples: The article promised *titillating* details about the actor.
There's nothing *titillating* about it — it's just gossip.
The show is *more titillating* than scary.

senses.gloss: Holding a title but not the real power.
examples: The queen is the *titular* head of state.
He's the *titular* president; the board runs everything.

senses.gloss: Named in the title of a book, movie or show.
examples: The *titular* character doesn't appear until the last act.
The novel takes its name from its *titular* lighthouse.

senses.gloss: Browned by heat, the way bread is in a toaster.
examples: I'll have a *toasted* bagel with cream cheese.
Sprinkle *toasted* almonds over the salad.
The bread was barely *toasted*.

contrast: As a noun a *token* is a coin-like piece or a sign of feeling; as an adjective it always means done only for show.

senses.gloss: Done only for show, and too small to matter.
examples: The company made a *token* effort to fix the problem.
They offered a *token* discount of two dollars.
She was the *token* woman on the committee.

senses.gloss: Bad, but not so bad that you cannot stand it.
examples: The heat is *tolerable* in the shade.
The food was *tolerable*, nothing more.
Music makes the drive *more tolerable*.

senses.gloss: Willing to accept beliefs and behavior different from your own.
examples: She's *tolerant* of people who disagree with her.
They raised their kids in a *tolerant* household.
He's *more tolerant* than he used to be.

senses.gloss: Able to stand a hard condition without being harmed.
examples: This variety is *tolerant* of cold weather.
We planted a drought-*tolerant* lawn.

senses.gloss: Costing the caller nothing, said of a phone number.
examples: Call our *toll-free* number for help.
The 800 number is *toll-free*.
Support is *toll-free* from anywhere in the country.

senses.gloss: Of a girl, behaving or dressing in ways people think of as boyish.
examples: She was a *tomboyish* kid who lived in jeans.
Her style is a little *tomboyish*.
The haircut looks *more tomboyish* than she wanted.

ru: лишённый музыкального слуха; не чувствующий настроения людей

senses.gloss: Unable to hear the difference between musical notes.
examples: I love singing, but I'm completely *tone-deaf*.
He's *tone-deaf*, so the choir was never an option.

senses.gloss: Badly out of touch with how other people feel.
examples: The ad was *tone-deaf* about the layoffs.
Her apology came across as *tone-deaf*.
It was the *most tone-deaf* thing he could have said.

senses.gloss: Of muscles or a body, firm from exercise.
examples: Her arms are *toned* from swimming.
He has a lean, *toned* build.
She's *more toned* now than she was a year ago.

senses.gloss: Said as a joke, even though it sounds serious.
examples: The whole review was *tongue-in-cheek*.
He made a *tongue-in-cheek* suggestion that we all quit.
Her thank-you speech was *tongue-in-cheek* from start to finish.

senses.gloss: Unable to speak because you are shy or nervous.
senses.ru: лишившийся дара речи, косноязычный от смущения
examples: I get *tongue-tied* whenever she's in the room.
He was so *tongue-tied* he forgot his own name.
Don't be *tongue-tied* — just tell them what happened.

senses.gloss: Having no teeth.
examples: The baby gave us a *toothless* grin.
An old, *toothless* dog slept by the fire.

senses.gloss: Having no real power to act.
examples: The new rules are *toothless* without penalties.
Critics called the committee *toothless*.
The law is *more toothless* than the one it replaced.

senses.gloss: Showing a lot of teeth, said of a smile.
examples: He flashed a *toothy* grin for the camera.
The mascot has a big *toothy* smile.
She gave the *toothiest* smile in the whole photo.

position: attributive only — *the top shelf*; after a verb use *on top* or *the best*
contrast: As a noun *a top* is the highest part or a piece of clothing; as a verb *to top* means to beat or to cover.

senses.gloss: Highest in place.
examples: The cereal is on the *top* shelf.
We stayed on the *top* floor.

senses.gloss: Best or most important.
examples: She's the *top* student in her class.
Safety is our *top* priority.
They hired a *top* lawyer from Chicago.

senses.gloss: Decided by the people in charge and passed down to everyone else.
examples: The change was *top-down*, with no input from the staff.
He runs the company in a *top-down* style.
They took a *top-down* approach to the budget.

senses.gloss: Of the very best quality or rank.
examples: They put together a *top-flight* research team.
She got *top-flight* medical care.
The school attracts *top-flight* coaches.

senses.gloss: So heavy at the top that it tips over easily.
examples: The bookcase is *top-heavy* — bolt it to the wall.
Don't load the cart that way; it gets *top-heavy*.

senses.gloss: Having too many managers for the number of workers.
examples: The company is *top-heavy* with vice presidents.
A *top-heavy* organization is slow to move.

senses.gloss: Excellent; of the highest quality.
examples: The service at that hotel is *top-notch*.
She's a *top-notch* editor.
We got *top-notch* seats for the game.

senses.gloss: Kept secret at the highest official level.
examples: The files are *top-secret*.
He had *top-secret* clearance for years.
It's a *top-secret* project — nobody will say a word about it.

senses.gloss: About something people are talking about right now.
examples: The show's humor is very *topical*.
She writes *topical* essays about the news.

senses.gloss: Put on the skin rather than swallowed.
examples: The doctor prescribed a *topical* cream.
*Topical* treatments work only where you rub them in.

senses.gloss: Wearing nothing above the waist, or allowing that.
examples: Some of the beaches there are *topless*.
*Topless* sunbathing is common on that coast.
The club advertised *topless* dancers.

senses.gloss: Turned upside down; in complete disorder.
examples: The move left the whole house *topsy-turvy*.
It's been a *topsy-turvy* year for the team.
Everything felt *topsy-turvy* after the news.

senses.gloss: Suffering deep mental pain.
examples: He was *tormented* by guilt for years.
The novel follows a *tormented* young artist.
She looked *more tormented* every time we spoke.

senses.gloss: Of rain, falling very hard and in huge amounts.
examples: *Torrential* rain closed the highway.
We drove through a *torrential* downpour.
*Torrential* storms flooded the valley.

senses.gloss: Very hot and dry.
examples: They crossed the *torrid* desert at night.
August brought *torrid* heat to the city.

senses.gloss: Full of strong sexual feeling.
examples: The tabloids described a *torrid* romance.
It was a *torrid* affair that lasted one summer.

contrast: *Tortuous* means twisting; *torturous* means full of pain. One letter apart, and Americans mix them up too.

senses.gloss: Full of twists and turns.
examples: We took a *tortuous* mountain road.
The river follows a *tortuous* path to the sea.

senses.gloss: Long, complicated and hard to follow.
examples: After *tortuous* negotiations, they finally signed.
His explanation was *tortuous* and full of side stories.

senses.gloss: Deeply unhappy; full of mental pain.
examples: He gave a *tortured* look and said nothing.
The band's songs are full of *tortured* love.

senses.gloss: Twisted into something forced and unnatural.
examples: That's a *tortured* reading of the rules.
He offered a *tortured* explanation for the missing money.

contrast: Not *tortuous*, which means twisting. *Torturous* is about pain.

senses.gloss: Causing great pain or suffering.
examples: The last mile of the run was *torturous*.
They sat through a *torturous* three-hour meeting.
Waiting for the results was *more torturous* than the test itself.

position: both — *a totaled car*; *The car was totaled*
form: -ed from the American verb *total*, to wreck beyond repair
contrast: American spelling with one *l*; the British write *totalled*. Used almost only about vehicles.

senses.gloss: Of a vehicle, wrecked so badly that repair would cost more than it is worth.
examples: Her car was *totaled* in the crash.
The insurance company declared the truck *totaled*.
He bought a *totaled* sedan for parts.

senses.gloss: Of a government that controls every part of life and allows no opposition.
examples: They grew up under a *totalitarian* regime.
The novel imagines a *totalitarian* future.
By the second year the state was openly *totalitarian*.

position: predicative only — *It was touch-and-go for a while*

senses.gloss: Uncertain and risky, so that it could still go either way.
examples: It was *touch-and-go* for a while, but she pulled through.
The landing was *touch-and-go* in that wind.
Funding for next year is still *touch-and-go*.

senses.gloss: Easily offended.
examples: He's *touchy* about his height.
Don't tease her — she gets *touchier* when she's tired.

senses.gloss: Of a subject or situation, needing careful handling.
examples: Money is a *touchy* subject in that family.
We're in a *touchy* spot with the landlord.

contrast: Usually disapproving — too much hugging or too much talk about feelings.

senses.gloss: Involving a lot of touching or open talk about feelings, often more than you want.
examples: The workshop was too *touchy-feely* for me.
He's not a *touchy-feely* kind of boss.
Her family is *more touchy-feely* than mine.

contrast: Glass treated this way is usually called *tempered* in American English, not *toughened*.

senses.gloss: Made stronger or harder, by hard experience or by treatment.
examples: He came back *toughened* by the experience.
A *toughened* veteran of two campaigns, she didn't flinch.
The steel is *toughened* to resist cracking.

contrast: Disapproving. The neutral word is *tourist* before a noun: *a tourist attraction*.

senses.gloss: Full of tourists and tourist shops, and not very real.
examples: That part of the city is too *touristy*.
We looked for a restaurant that wasn't *touristy*.
The beach gets *more touristy* every summer.

senses.gloss: Of hair, messy in a casual way.
examples: He showed up with *tousled* hair and no jacket.
She has that *tousled* just-woke-up look.
His hair was *tousled* from the wind.

senses.gloss: Very tall and rising high above everything around.
examples: *Towering* pines lined the road.
They live under a *towering* cliff.

senses.gloss: Far greater than others in importance.
examples: She was a *towering* figure in American poetry.
Building it in one year was a *towering* achievement.

senses.gloss: Poisonous; able to harm or kill.
examples: The plant gives off *toxic* fumes.
These paints are *toxic* if swallowed.

senses.gloss: Making the people around it unhappy or harmed.
examples: She finally left a *toxic* relationship.
The office culture had turned *toxic*.
Nothing is *more toxic* than a boss who lies to you.

senses.gloss: Able to be followed back to a source.
examples: The leak was *traceable* to one email account.
Every part they use is *traceable*.
Cash isn't *traceable* the way a card is.

senses.gloss: Able to be followed while it moves or happens.
examples: Ship it with a *trackable* number.
The package is *trackable* online.
Every click on the site is *trackable*.

contrast: Formal. The opposite, *intractable*, is far more common in everyday writing.

senses.gloss: Easy to control or manage.
examples: The pony is *tractable* enough for beginners.
He gets *more tractable* after lunch.

senses.gloss: Of a problem, simple enough to be worked out.
examples: Break the job into *tractable* pieces.
The question is hard but *tractable*.

senses.gloss: Registered as a company's legal name or symbol.
examples: The name is *trademarked*, so you can't use it.
They sell it under a *trademarked* brand.
*Trademarked* logos can't be copied onto your own shirts.

senses.gloss: Following the customs and ways that have been handed down.
examples: We had a *traditional* Thanksgiving dinner.
Her parents are *traditional* about weddings.
This neighborhood is *more traditional* than downtown.

contrast: More often a noun (*He's a traditionalist*); as an adjective it describes people and views that hold to the old ways.

senses.gloss: Holding to old ways and against change.
examples: The change upset the *traditionalist* wing of the party.
He takes a *traditionalist* view of the ceremony.
*Traditionalist* parishes kept the older service.

senses.gloss: Very sad, especially because of death or loss.
examples: It was a *tragic* accident.
The *most tragic* part is that it could have been prevented.

senses.gloss: Belonging to tragedy as a kind of drama.
examples: He played the *tragic* hero.
The play has a *tragic* ending.

senses.gloss: Taught the skills that a job or task needs.
examples: All our staff are *trained* in first aid.
She's a *trained* nurse.
The dogs are *trained* to find survivors.

senses.gloss: Calm, quiet and peaceful.
examples: We found a *tranquil* spot by the lake.
The house is *tranquil* in the early morning.
Nothing is *more tranquil* than that little garden.

senses.gloss: Crossing the Atlantic, or between North America and Europe.
examples: We took a *transatlantic* flight to Lisbon.
The two labs have a *transatlantic* partnership.
*Transatlantic* trade talks resumed in May.

senses.gloss: Going far beyond ordinary limits; extraordinary.
examples: Her performance was *transcendent*.
He talked about a *transcendent* moment on the mountain.
The last song was the *most transcendent* part of the night.

senses.gloss: Crossing a whole continent.
examples: The *transcontinental* railroad changed the country.
They made a *transcontinental* drive in five days.
It's a *transcontinental* flight, so pack a snack.

senses.gloss: Able to be passed from one person, place or job to another.
examples: The ticket is not *transferable*.
She has *transferable* skills that any office would want.
The credits are *transferable* to a state school.

contrast: An adjective only — *a transgender student*, never a noun. Do not add *-ed*.

senses.gloss: Having a gender identity different from the sex recorded at birth.
examples: She is *transgender* and uses she and her.
The school has a policy for *transgender* students.
He came out as *transgender* last year.

contrast: As a noun *a transient* is a person with no fixed home.

senses.gloss: Lasting only a short time.
examples: The pain was *transient* and passed by morning.
Fame like that is *transient*.

senses.gloss: Staying only briefly in a place.
examples: The motel serves a *transient* population.
It's a *transient* neighborhood — people move every year.

senses.gloss: Belonging to the stage between one situation and the next.
examples: She's in a *transitional* period between jobs.
They set up a *transitional* government.
The housing is *transitional*, not permanent.

senses.gloss: Of a verb, taking a direct object.
examples: *Hit* is a *transitive* verb: you hit something.
Many verbs are both *transitive* and intransitive.
The dictionary marks every *transitive* use with a label.

contrast: Formal; in speech Americans say *temporary* or *short-lived*.

senses.gloss: Lasting only a short time.
examples: Economists called the price jump *transitory*.
It was a *transitory* phase in her career.
Happiness like that is *transitory*.

senses.gloss: Able to be put into another language or form.
examples: That joke isn't *translatable* into English.
The poem is barely *translatable*.
His lab results are *translatable* to human medicine.

contrast: *Translucent* lets light through but you can't see through it clearly; *transparent* you can see right through.

senses.gloss: Letting light through without being clear.
examples: The bathroom window is *translucent*.
She used *translucent* paper for the lampshade.
The petals are thin and *translucent*.

senses.gloss: Able to be passed from one person or animal to another.
examples: The disease is *transmissible* through the air.
The new variant is *more transmissible* than the last one.
It's *transmissible* to dogs but not to cats.

senses.gloss: Working across several countries rather than tied to one.
examples: *Transnational* corporations moved in first.
It's a *transnational* problem that no one country can fix.
She studies *transnational* labor movements.

senses.gloss: Clear enough to see through.
examples: The container is *transparent*, so you can see what's inside.
*Transparent* tape doesn't show on the paper.

senses.gloss: Open about what is being done, hiding nothing.
examples: The city promised a *more transparent* budget process.
We try to be *transparent* with customers about prices.

senses.gloss: So obvious that nobody is fooled.
examples: It was a *transparent* attempt to change the subject.
His excuse was *transparent*.

senses.gloss: Able to be carried or moved from place to place.
examples: The extra classroom is a *transportable* unit.
The patient wasn't *transportable* until the next day.
We need a *transportable* generator for the job site.

ru: пойманный в ловушку; загнанный в угол
position: both — mostly after a verb (*He felt trapped*)

senses.gloss: Caught somewhere with no way out.
examples: Two workers were *trapped* under the rubble.
We were *trapped* in the elevator for an hour.

senses.gloss: Unable to escape a life or situation you hate.
senses.ru: загнанный в угол, как в ловушке
examples: She felt *trapped* in the marriage.
A *trapped* feeling came over him at his desk.

senses.gloss: Cheap and of poor quality, especially in taste.
examples: I read *trashy* novels at the beach.
The show is *trashy* but fun.
Her taste in movies is *trashier* than mine.

senses.gloss: Causing lasting emotional shock, or caused by a physical injury.
examples: The accident was *traumatic* for the whole family.
He suffered a *traumatic* brain injury.
Moving was *more traumatic* for the kids than for us.

contrast: American spelling with one *l*; the British write *travelled*.

senses.gloss: Having traveled a lot and seen many places.
examples: She's a widely *traveled* journalist.
He's the *most traveled* person I know.

senses.gloss: Of a road, used by many people.
examples: Take the less *traveled* road along the river.
It's a heavily *traveled* stretch of highway.

senses.gloss: Dangerous, especially when the danger is hidden.
examples: The roads are *treacherous* after an ice storm.
They climbed a *treacherous* slope in the dark.
The current gets *more treacherous* near the rocks.

senses.gloss: Betraying someone who trusts you.
examples: It was a *treacherous* thing to do to a friend.
His *treacherous* deputy went straight to the press.

senses.gloss: Amounting to betrayal of your own country.
examples: The letters were called *treasonous*.
He was charged with *treasonous* acts.
Selling those plans would be *treasonous*.

senses.gloss: Kept and loved because it means a great deal to you.
examples: The ring is a *treasured* family heirloom.
Those letters are among her *most treasured* possessions.
He keeps a *treasured* photo of his grandfather on the desk.

senses.gloss: Shaking slightly, usually from cold, fear or strong feeling.
examples: She signed the paper with a *trembling* hand.
His voice was *trembling*.
The puppy stood *trembling* in the rain.

senses.gloss: Very large in amount, degree or force.
examples: It took a *tremendous* amount of work.
There was a *tremendous* crash from the kitchen.

senses.gloss: Excellent.
examples: You did a *tremendous* job on that report.
The band was *tremendous* live.

senses.gloss: Of comment or criticism, sharp, clear and forceful.
examples: She wrote a *trenchant* analysis of the ruling.
His *trenchant* criticism stung.
The review raised the *most trenchant* objection yet.

senses.gloss: Starting a style that others then copy.
examples: She's a *trendsetting* designer.
The phone had a *trendsetting* design.
*Trendsetting* restaurants opened all over the neighborhood.

contrast: Slightly disapproving — fashionable now, maybe not for long. Plain praise is *stylish*.

senses.gloss: Very fashionable at the moment.
examples: They opened a *trendy* coffee shop downtown.
That neighborhood gets *trendier* every year.
The jacket is *trendy* but not cheap.

contrast: Always capitalized, like the other geological periods (*Jurassic*, *Cretaceous*).

senses.gloss: Of the geological period before the Jurassic, when the first dinosaurs appeared.
examples: These fossils are from the *Triassic* period.
*Triassic* rock runs through the valley.
The first dinosaurs appeared in *Triassic* times.

senses.gloss: Hard to do or handle; needing care.
examples: Parallel parking on this street is *tricky*.
The wiring is the *trickiest* part of the job.

senses.gloss: Clever in a dishonest way.
examples: He's a *tricky* negotiator.
Watch out — that's a *tricky* question.

position: both — hyphenated before a noun: *a tried-and-true method*

senses.gloss: Tested many times and known to work.
examples: Her method is *tried and true*.
We went back to the *tried-and-true* recipe.
There's a *tried-and-true* way to fix this.

ru: готовый чуть что стрелять; скорый на расправу

senses.gloss: Too quick to shoot, or too quick to act without thinking.
examples: The movie's hero is *trigger-happy*.
A *trigger-happy* manager fires people over nothing.
He's *more trigger-happy* with the delete key than I am.

senses.gloss: Involving three countries or three sides.
examples: The three states signed a *trilateral* agreement.
*Trilateral* talks begin next week.
It's a *trilateral* deal, not a pair of separate ones.

senses.gloss: Speaking three languages, or written in three.
senses.ru: владеющий тремя языками; на трёх языках
examples: She's *trilingual* — English, Spanish and Korean.
The signs at the border are *trilingual*.
They run a *trilingual* preschool.

contrast: Also a verb (*trim the hedge*) and a noun (*white trim around the windows*).

senses.gloss: Slim and in good shape.
examples: He stays *trim* by running every morning.
She's *trimmer* now than she was in college.

senses.gloss: Neat and well kept.
examples: A row of *trim* little houses lined the street.
The yard was *trim* and green.

senses.gloss: Having three parts, or involving three groups.
examples: The essay has a *tripartite* structure.
They reached a *tripartite* agreement.
The board set up a *tripartite* review.

contrast: Also a verb (*prices tripled*) and, in baseball, a noun (*he hit a triple*).

senses.gloss: Having three parts, or three times as much.
examples: She ordered a *triple* espresso.
The recipe makes a *triple* batch.
They charged him in a *triple* homicide.

comparison: -er/-est or more/most — *triter* or *more trite*, *tritest* or *most trite*

senses.gloss: Used so often that it has lost all its force.
examples: The ending felt *trite*.
That advice is *trite* but true.
Nothing sounds *more trite* than a speech about following your dreams.

senses.gloss: Having won, and showing great joy about it.
examples: The team made a *triumphant* return home.
She looked *triumphant* when the numbers came in.
He gave a *triumphant* shout from the other room.

contrast: A false friend: *trivial* means unimportant, not banal or obvious. For those say *trite* or *obvious*.

senses.gloss: So small or unimportant that it isn't worth attention.
examples: They argue over *trivial* things.
The bug is *trivial* — it can wait until Monday.
Nothing about her health is *trivial* to him.

senses.gloss: Of, from, or like the hot wet regions near the equator.
examples: We spent a week on a *tropical* island.
The plant needs *tropical* humidity.
A *tropical* storm is forming off the coast.

senses.gloss: Having no problems; working without trouble.
examples: The car gave us ten *trouble-free* years.
The install was completely *trouble-free*.
Nothing is entirely *trouble-free*.
